children: EU new passenger car registrations rose 4.5% Y/Y to 708,200 units in August, extending the market’s growth streak to seven consecutive months as demand for EVs remained strong, the ACEA reported on Thursday.

August growth accelerated from a 3% increase in July, with the EU’s four largest car markets all recording gains. Spain posted the strongest increase at 11.8%, followed by France at 7.4%, Italy at 3.2%, and Germany at 2.6%.

For the first eight months of 2026, new EU car registrations increased 5.3% despite persistent geopolitical uncertainty and rising energy prices. ACEA said demand for EVs continued to benefit from market support measures and a broader range of available models.

BEVs accounted for 21.7% of new EU car registrations through August, up from 15.8% a year earlier, highlighting the continued shift toward electrification. Hybrids held the largest share at 36.6%, and plug-in hybrids 10%.

Among major markets, BEV registrations increased 74.2% in France, 53.1% in Germany, and 40.9% in Denmark in the first eight months of 2026. France, Germany, and Denmark together accounted for 64% of total EU BEV registrations during the period.
YTD, Chinese automakers continued to post strong gains in the EU. Chery Automobile
rose 250.9% to 116,318 units, while BYD Company
increased 163% to 177,752 units. Tesla
sales climbed 65.9% to 142,165 units, while SAIC Motor gained 19.8% to 163,707 units and Geely Group rose 7.8% to 205,047 units. Among major traditional automakers, Volkswagen Group
rose 1.3% to 1.99M units, and Stellantis
increased 5.2% to 1.20M units, while Ford Motor
fell 17.7%, Renault Group
declined 4%, and Hyundai (HYMTF) dropped 2.2%.
